new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Not priced under another name: parmesan is a different aged cheese and price, mozzarella-cheese and provolone-cheese are fresh/semi-soft at half the per-oz price, and the bagged shredded-cheese id is cheddar/blend. Captures carry Asiago wedges today, so a null would pantry-price half a pound of specialty cheese.

registrar_rulings.reason: No id in commodities.json, recipe-commodities.json, or recipe-board-everyday.json carries asiago, and a -o context grep of the minified smp-feed.json finds zero asiago product strings, so it is neither existing nor priced under any name; the estate's only 'asiago' occurrence is pecorino-romano's own EXCLUDE (commodities.json:67101), which is positive evidence the near hard-cheese ids deliberately refuse it, and parmesan/pecorino/gruyere are different aged cheeses (different food, not a spelling). Mint asiago-cheese (kebab-case, generic, 'asiago' survives contiguously in real product names) in the weekly commodities.json + capture worklist since today's captures carry Asiago wedges. FOLLOW-UP EDITS: (1) include ~ '\basiago(?:\s+cheese)?\b'; (2) build a full-rigor exclude list (~150 patterns, copy pecorino-romano's block as the base) and specifically exclude asiago bagels/bread/crackers, dressings/dips/sauces, snack blends, and parmesan-asiago / romano-asiago BLEND shreds so a blend never crowns the wedge; (3) add commodity-dupe-allowlist.json pairs asiago-cheese<->parmesan, asiago-cheese<->pecorino-romano, asiago-cheese<->gruyere (same food family, different aged cheese = different purchase) so the daily audit never re-flags them; (4) note block-cheese's 'cheese\s+block' include could claim an 'Asiago Cheese Block' product name - add '\basiago\b' to block-cheese's excludes; (5) separately, add the vocabulary row 'Asiago Cheese' in meal-prep\db\ingredients.json resolving to this id - the name mint and the id mint are two acts and both are needed, neither exists today.
